title: Cutting, Punching, and Press Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to saw, cut, shear, slit, punch, crimp, notch, bend, or straighten metal or plastic material.

tasks.text: Measure completed workpieces to verify conformance to specifications, using micrometers, gauges, calipers, templates, or rulers.
Examine completed workpieces for defects, such as chipped edges or marred surfaces and sort defective pieces according to types of flaws.
Read work orders or production schedules to determine specifications, such as materials to be used, locations of cutting lines, or dimensions and tolerances.
Start machines, monitor their operations, and record operational data.
Set up, operate, or tend machines to saw, cut, shear, slit, punch, crimp, notch, bend, or straighten metal or plastic material.
Test and adjust machine speeds or actions, according to product specifications, using gauges and hand tools.
Load workpieces, plastic material, or chemical solutions into machines.
Turn controls to set cutting speeds, feed rates, or table angles for specified operations.
Clean work area.
Lubricate workpieces with oil.
Install, align, and lock specified punches, dies, cutting blades, or other fixtures in rams or beds of machines, using gauges, templates, feelers, shims, and hand tools.
Adjust ram strokes of presses to specified lengths, using hand tools.
Position, align, and secure workpieces against fixtures or stops on machine beds or on dies.
Set stops on machine beds, change dies, and adjust components, such as rams or power presses, when making multiple or successive passes.
Clean and lubricate machines.
Position guides, stops, holding blocks, or other fixtures to secure and direct workpieces, using hand tools and measuring devices.
Place workpieces on cutting tables, manually or using hoists, cranes, or sledges.
Replace defective blades or wheels, using hand tools.
Plan sequences of operations, applying knowledge of physical properties of workpiece materials.
Mark identifying data on workpieces.
Turn valves to start flow of coolant against cutting areas or to start airflow that blows cuttings away from kerfs.
Hone cutters with oilstones to remove nicks.
Remove housings, feed tubes, tool holders, or other accessories to replace worn or broken parts, such as springs or bushings.
Sharpen dulled blades, using bench grinders, abrasive wheels, or lathes.
Operate forklifts to deliver materials.
Select, clean, and install spacers, rubber sleeves, or cutters on arbors.
Scribe reference lines on workpieces as guides for cutting operations, according to blueprints, templates, sample parts, or specifications.
Grind out burrs or sharp edges, using portable grinders, speed lathes, or polishing jacks.
Set blade tensions, heights, and angles to perform prescribed cuts, using wrenches.
Use equipment designed to join sheet metal, such as spot welders.
Preheat workpieces, using heating furnaces or hand torches.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Operation and Control

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Troubleshooting

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making

skills.name: Reading Comprehension

skills.name: Active Learning

skills.name: Coordination

skills.name: Time Management

skills.name: Repairing

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: SAP software.
